method:
Geometry first, on prims 'bank2' (area L2). The wall model is the union of the solid hatches on A-WALL and A-WALL-PATT, the S-COLS column hatches, and the 100 mm bands of the five 'GLASS WALL 2600H' blocks. Every A-WALL outline line is covered by a hatch except the free-standing curved SE parapet and the glass-wall outlines. A dwgread dump of the original DWG gives the same A-WALL*/A-DOOR*/S-COLS entity counts as the DXF, so the 8 LibreDWG errors lost nothing relevant; the missing handles are inside dimension blocks.

For each of the 24 A-DOOR inserts (20 in the Revit host block, 4 at top level), I intersected the line through the insert point, along the block rotation, with the wall model. The gap around the insert is the structural opening; the frame lines lie inside it. Every insert sits at its opening centre on the wall centre line. The one exception is the rack door: the toilet wall crosses its frame (see uncertain).

I then searched for gaps between collinear wall pieces with no door, which found the toilet lobby mouth (B2-04), and listed free wall-end caps to catch other doorless gaps.

I reviewed 15 tiles of about 5x5 m (--grid 0.5 --inserts --px 2000): x [-6,-1], [-1.5,3.5], [3,8.5] by y [-11.5,-6.5], [-7,-2], [-2.5,2.5], [2,7], [6.5,12.5]. I also zoomed into the wealth room corners. The final checks were a full-level render with a marker at each opening and 5 zoomed marker renders (NW, NE, SE, SW, middle): every door leaf, arc and wall gap has a marker.

There are no windows on Level 2: no window blocks and no glazing layers. The facades are solid walls with louvred swing doors, and the only glazing is the wealth room's glass walls.
